name: Approvals
description: Sign-offs that gate states of the type's Workflow. A transition into a gated state, from a state its gate allows, waits until each of the gate's requirements that applies has as many distinct signers holding its permission as its count; the instance's creator cannot sign unless the requirement allows it. A gate is one requirement written in the config, or reads its requirements from the rows of a type that each instance writes (requirementsFrom). A requirement may also name which callers it counts, the proof each sign-off shows, whom it excludes and when it applies. A change of the instance's own fields consumes every gate's sign-offs, unless the config keeps them, and entering a gated state consumes that gate's, so a return to it signs again. Consumed sign-offs stay listed. Deleting the instance deletes its sign-offs.

gates.description: The gates, by the state of the type's Workflow each gates.

count.description: How many distinct signers must sign off before a transition into the state. Needed unless the gate reads its requirements from rows.

permission.description: The permission a caller needs to sign off. Needed unless the gate reads its requirements from rows.

from.description: The states of the type's Workflow a transition from is gated; every state when absent.

excludeCreator.description: Whether the principal who created the instance is refused a sign-off; true when absent.

resetOn.description: The own fields whose change, by an update, consumes the gate's sign-offs; [] for none. Absent, the gate follows resetOnChange. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

pinned.description: Whether a sign-off names the row's version its signer read: signOff then needs version, and one that is not the row's version is vetoed stale. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

pinOn.description: Own fields a sign-off is pinned to: signOff then names in read the value of each as its signer read it, and one that is not the field's value is vetoed stale. Unlike pinned, a write to another field does not make a signer stale. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

callers.description: Which callers count, and as whom: person, a person calling as themselves; acting-for-person, an agent run acting for a person, counted as that person; agent, an agent run, counted as its Agent. Every caller counts, as its subject, when absent. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

proof.description: What each sign-off shows, as the host reports the caller's assurance: none; recent-sign-in, a sign-in at most proofWithinMs before it; user-verification, a passkey with user verification on the sign-off itself. none when absent. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

proofWithinMs.description: For recent-sign-in, the most milliseconds a sign-in may come before the sign-off. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

excludeCreatorPerson.description: Whether the person the creator acted for, the subject the type's own field createdFor holds, is refused a sign-off too; false when absent. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

excludeSubjectsIn.description: Own fields that list subjects, persons and Agents who may not sign: a caller is excluded when its subject, the person it acts for or its run's Agent is listed. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

recheckPermission.description: Whether each transition the gate guards reads each signer's permission again, so a signer who has lost it stops counting; false when absent, which reads it at the sign-off. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

when.description: The conditions on the instance's own fields under which the requirement applies, all of them; it always applies when absent. A requirement that does not apply asks for nothing, and a condition on a field with no value makes it apply. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

field.description: An own field of the instance.

test.description: every-matches: every value of the field matches one of the glob patterns; any-matches: one value does; contains: the field holds one of the values; at-most: the field's number is at most the one value.

values.description: The glob patterns (* within a path segment, ** across segments, ? one character), the values, or the one number.

negate.description: Whether the condition holds when its test fails; false when absent.

requirementsFrom.description: Reads the gate's requirements from the rows of a type, so each instance writes its own: the rows of schema whose to-one relation link points at the instance, or, with in, at one of the keys the instance's own list field in holds. A row holds a requirement's members as its own fields (count, permission, callers, proof, proofWithinMs, excludeCreator, excludeCreatorPerson, excludeSubjectsIn, recheckPermission, when) and may hold name, resetOn and archivedAt. An archived row asks for nothing. A row's resetOn spends a sign-off for that requirement alone: a sign-off records the value of each field the rows reset on, and counts for a requirement only while its fields still hold them. The gate then names none of the requirement's members, and names its own resetOn. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

schema.description: The type whose rows are the requirements.

link.description: The to-one relation of schema's rows the rows are found by.

in.description: An own list field of the instance that holds the keys link points at; absent, link points at the instance itself.

resetOnChange.description: Whether a change of the instance's own fields, an update or an operation's, consumes every gate's sign-offs; true when absent.

status.description: The field of the type whose Workflow the gates are of. Implied when the type has one Workflow; needed when it has several. A Workflow anchored on the type is named Workflow. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

fields.name: gates
fields.description: The sign-offs not yet consumed, by gated state: { <state>: { signedBy } }, each subject that signed, in the order they signed; a gate with none is absent.

operations.name: signOff
operations.description: Signs off on the instance for a gated state, as the caller. Needs the permission of one of the gate's requirements, and is refused unless it counts toward one of them now: for the instance's creator unless the requirement allows it, for a caller the requirement does not count, excludes or whose proof falls short, while the instance is in the state, and for a caller whose sign-off for the state is not yet consumed.

state.description: The gated state to sign off for.

version.description: The row's version the signer read, the version a write through the core is held to. Needed on a pinned gate; on any gate, one that is not the row's version is vetoed stale before anything else is checked. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

read.description: The value of each field the gate pins (pinOn) as the signer read it, by field. Needed on a gate that pins fields; one that is not the field's value is vetoed stale before anything else is checked. A table's alone: an engine type refuses it.

resultSchema.description: The sign-off, with the gate's sign-offs after it and the count it needs.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

signedBy.description: Every subject whose sign-off for the state is not yet consumed, in the order they signed.

count.description: How many the gate needs: its count, or for a gate that reads its requirements from rows, the count of the first requirement the sign-off counts toward.

countsToward.description: For a gate that reads its requirements from rows, the name of each requirement the sign-off counts toward now.

operations.name: withdrawSignOff
operations.description: Withdraws the caller's sign-off for a gated state, one not yet consumed.

state.description: The gated state whose sign-off to withdraw.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

actingFor.description: The subject the caller acted for.

agent.description: The Agent whose run the caller was.

at.description: When it was signed, in epoch milliseconds.

operations.name: listSignOffs
operations.description: Lists the instance's sign-offs, oldest first, one page at a time, the consumed ones included; with state, only those for it.

limit.description: At most this many sign-offs; 50 when absent.

cursor.description: The next of the previous page.

subject.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

actingFor.description: The subject the caller acted for.

agent.description: The Agent whose run the caller was.

consumedAt.description: When a change of the own fields, entering the state or a new version without its gate consumed it; absent while it counts.

next.description: The cursor of the next page; null after the last.

vetoes.description: A transition into a gated state, from a state its gate allows, while a requirement that applies has fewer sign-offs than its count; details give the state, the count required and the sign-offs it has, and for a gate that reads its requirements from rows each requirement it misses.
signOff by a caller whose sign-off for the state is not yet consumed.
signOff by the principal who created the instance, when every requirement whose permission the caller holds excludes the creator.
signOff while the instance is in the gated state.
signOff or withdrawSignOff for a state the config does not gate.

signOff by a caller whose sign-off would count toward none of the gate's requirements whose permission it holds: none counts its kind of caller, it excludes the caller, or its proof falls short; details give each requirement's reason.
withdrawSignOff by a caller with no sign-off for the state that is not yet consumed.

signOff naming a version that is not the row's version, or a value of a pinned field that is not the field's value: what the signer read has moved since; details give what it named and what is current. A table's alone: an engine type refuses version and read.

tables.name: signOffs
tables.description: One row per sign-off on the row, keyed by its number, the order it was given in: the gated state, the caller who signed (its subject and kind, whom it acted for and its run's Agent), the assurance its host reported, the permissions it held and the values of the fields the gate's requirements reset on, why, when, and when it was consumed, absent while it counts. A withdrawal deletes its row; consumed ones stay for listSignOffs.

fields.name: number
fields.description: The sign-off's number on the row, from 1 in the order they were given, in ten digits zero-padded so the key's order is theirs.

fields.name: state
fields.description: The gated state it signs off for.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: The subject of the caller who signed.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: The caller's kind (D156): user, party, agent or extension; absent when the host named none.

fields.name: actingFor
fields.description: The subject the caller acted for (D77); absent when it acted for no one.

fields.name: actingForKind
fields.description: The kind of the subject the caller acted for; absent when the host named none.

fields.name: agent
fields.description: The Agent whose run the caller was (D158); absent for a caller that was no agent run.

fields.name: signedInAt
fields.description: When the caller's session last signed in, as its host reported it.

fields.name: userVerified
fields.description: Whether the caller proved user verification on the sign-off itself.

fields.name: held
fields.description: The permissions the caller held when it signed, a list, which a requirement read from rows counts unless it reads them again.

fields.name: values
fields.description: The value each field the gate's requirements reset on held when it signed, by field, null for none.

fields.name: at
fields.description: When it was given, in epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: consumedAt
fields.description: When a change of the fields its gate names, an entry into the gated state or a build without its gate consumed it; absent while it counts.
